title: Synthesizing Signals to Decide Whether to Release a Held Vendor Payment
scenario_text:
An accounts-payable controls agent at Thornton Manufacturing must decide whether to release a $268,000 payment that the fraud-screening rule flagged for review.

**NetSuite (AP) — Invoice INV-55120**
Vendor: 'Delmarva Industrial Supply' | Amount: $268,000 | Matches PO-9982 (3-way match passed: PO, receipt, invoice) | Payment method: ACH.

**Bank change log (Treasury system)**
Vendor remit-to bank was updated 4 days ago from 'Keystone Bank acct ...3320' to 'Sunbelt Trust acct ...7741'. Change requested via inbound email; no callback verification recorded.

**Email trail (AP inbox)**
- 4 days ago, from 'accounts@delmarva-supply.com': 'Please update our banking for all future payments; new details attached. Urgent — remit the open invoice to the new account.' Sender domain is delmarva-supply.com. The vendor's verified domain on file is delmarvaindustrial.com.

**Vendor master (verified contacts)**
AP contact of record: Karen Doyle, phone on file. Verified email domain: delmarvaindustrial.com.

**Slack — #ap-controls**
AP clerk: 'Invoice is legit — the 3-way match is clean and the PO is real. The only new thing is the bank update. Can I release it to the new account?'

The agent must weigh a legitimate underlying invoice against the payment-integrity signals.
question: What should the agent do with the $268,000 payment?
choices: Release the payment to the new Sunbelt Trust account — the 3-way match passed and the invoice is legitimate, so the payment is valid
Hold the payment and reject only the invoice — the clean 3-way match is irrelevant once any anomaly appears
Release the payment but to the old Keystone Bank account on file, ignoring the bank-change request

Hold the payment, do not remit to the new account, and verify the bank-change request out-of-band by calling Karen Doyle at the phone number on file — the mismatched sender domain and unverified bank change are classic business-email-compromise indicators independent of the invoice's validity
